model_annotations.English: Figure 5 presents a bar chart comparing per-output and per-layer perplexity values across different sparsity rates (10% to 80%), as derived from Table 13, which is displayed above the figure. The horizontal axis lists the sparsity rates (10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, 80%) in ascending order, while the vertical axis represents perplexity on a logarithmic scale, as noted in the figure caption, due to the large range of values between low and high sparsity. Two sets of bars are shown for each sparsity level: one for “Per-Output” (light blue) and one for “Per-Layer” (orange). At lower sparsity rates (e.g., 10%–40%), both methods yield similar perplexity values (ranging from ~5.7 to ~6.5). However, as sparsity increases beyond 50%, the perplexity for both methods rises sharply, with “Per-Layer” consistently showing higher values than “Per-Output” at each sparsity level — for instance, at 80% sparsity, “Per-Output” reaches 534.42 while “Per-Layer” reaches 886.10. The bars are grouped by sparsity rate, with “Per-Output” bars positioned to the left of “Per-Layer” bars within each group, and the height of each bar visually reflects the magnitude of the perplexity value on the log scale. The chart’s visual emphasis is on the diverging performance between the two pruning strategies as sparsity increases, with the logarithmic scaling allowing both low and high values to be represented meaningfully within the same plot.
